messages:
Anya K.: Quick follow-up on the retry/idempotency shape for pagination + streams — leaning into either server-issued lease tokens or client nonces. Need SDK tradeoffs (py/ts/go) + transport implications. Thoughts?
Sam B.: My take: server lease token sounds cleaner for multi-page operations. Server can mark cursor consumed. TTL avoids long locks. But it adds state to infra.
Matt L.: Client nonce is simplest for SDKs. Generate a uuid per operation, send on every request, server dedups. No infra RPCs to fetch token. Still requires storing seen nonces (stateful) but simpler ergonomics.
Liam R.: We should avoid per-request DB ops at high throughput. Idea: lease tokens embedded in cursor and verified with HMAC instead of storing server-side. Stateless verification.
Anya K.: HMAC cursor = neat. How do SDKs surface key-rotation or verification failures? We need a transparent retry story.
Sam B.: SDKs can auto-retry once on a verification failure by obtaining a fresh cursor/lease. In TS/Py do it by default; Go could expose a small helper so runtime stays explicit.
Matt L.: Ergonomics note: Python/TS teams prefer opinionated defaults. Go team wants minimal magic. Expect bikeshedding.
Liam R.: Transport nuance: streaming (grpc/ws) can hold ephemeral server state tied to connection and issue short leases there. For unary HTTP, prefer signed cursor or client nonce to remain stateless.
Anya K.: Proposal sketch:
1) Add `X-RWD-LEASE` response header (optional) for server-issued lease blobs.
2) Add `X-RWD-OP-NONCE` request header for client-generated idempotency nonces.
3) Cursor blob may include an opt `signed_lease` base64 token.
SDK default priority: stream-lease > signed-cursor > client-nonce.
Matt L.: Example usage (pseudo):
```
# request
X-RWD-OP-NONCE: 3f2a-4f9b-...-uuid
# response
X-RWD-LEASE: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... (base64)
```
Sam B.: :+1: Let's version headers (eg `X-RWD-LEASE-v1`) and add telemetry for retries/dedups. Need to avoid quietly dropping user ops.
Anya K.: Action items I will work into RFC:
- Py/TS: implement auto-retry 1x for nonce/signature failures, provide opt-out flag (sdk.retry.auto_idempotency)
- Go: provide helper `WithIdempotencyNonce()` and explicit examples
- Runtime: support signed-cursor verification + key-rotation endpoint and clear error codes for invalid/expired leases
- API: header names + examples + backward compatibility notes
I'll open draft RFC + PR.
ci-bot: CI passed on draft-rfc branch #4567 :white_check_mark:
Liam R.: Edge-case: pagination over evolving indexes (non-monotonic cursors). Server must reject stale signed-cursor; fallback is client restart from page 1 or resume via server-side scan. Document fallback.
Matt L.: :thinking: Also consider cross-region retries — signed lease should include region tag or TTL bound to region.
Sam B.: I'll prototype TS helper this week and post a short demo branch: https://git.internal/rwd/ts-sdk/pull/789 (WIP).
Anya K.: Cool. If no objections I'll publish RFC tomorrow EOD. :rocket:
